results.title: Rapid detection of monkeypox virus using a CRISPR-Cas12a mediated assay: a laboratory validation and evaluation study
results.content: MPXV-CRISPR fluorescence assays included three types of control samples: no-template control, no-guide control, and at least one non-MPXV viral gDNA control (appendix 2 p 600148-9/fulltext#supplementary-material)). We developed an assay encompassing RPA in combination with CRISPR-Cas12a-mediated DNA target recognition and ssDNA cleavage (referred to as MPXV-CRISPR), coupled with high throughput fluorescence-based and lateral-flow strip readouts (appendix 1 p 900148-9/fulltext#supplementary-material)). To determine the LOD of MPXV-CRISPR, we compared background-corrected fluorescence of the MPXV dilution series with no-template control at 40 min and found that set 7D, which targeted a non-genic region present in two copies (appendix 1 p 1100148-9/fulltext#supplementary-material)), displayed the highest sensitivity (LOD of 1 genome copy per μL), while sets 5E and 6B had a LOD of 100 genome copies per μL (figure 1B00148-9/fulltext#fig1), appendix 1 p 1600148-9/fulltext#supplementary-material)). Assay precision testing was performed using set 7D and dilution series of MPXV gDNA, control gDNA (herpes simplex virus type 1 and varicella zoster virus), and no-template control (appendix 1 pp 6, 1800148-9/fulltext#supplementary-material)). To further validate our assay, we performed blinded concordance testing on gDNA from 185 clinical samples (85 from skin lesions, 55 from the anus, 44 from the oral cavity, and one from the nasopharynx; appendix 2 p 300148-9/fulltext#supplementary-material)), comparing MPXV-CRISPR with an in-house qPCR assay targeting the hemagglutinin gene.1600148-9/fulltext#). The MPXV-CRISPR assay correctly identified all positive samples, with fluorescence signal above no-template control background detectable within the first 5 min of the assay (figure 2A00148-9/fulltext#fig2); appendix 2 p 300148-9/fulltext#supplementary-material)). To assess the compatibility of the MPXV-CRISPR assay with a lateral-flow detection method, we repeated analytical and clinical sensitivity and specificity testing immediately after the fluorescence-based assay on lateral-flow strips, made possible by the dual-labelled reporter (figure 300148-9/fulltext#fig3); appendix 1 pp 20–2100148-9/fulltext#supplementary-material)). Consistent with the fluorescence-based assay, and using either manual inspection or computational image analysis, lateral-flow readouts with set 7D achieved an LOD of 1 copy per μL and 100% specificity for MPXV, with no cross-reactivity against a specificity panel of other viruses, including other poxviruses (figure 3B, C00148-9/fulltext#fig3); appendix 1 pp 22–2300148-9/fulltext#supplementary-material)). This positivity threshold was applied to lateral-flow testing using the 185 clinical samples described above (figure 3E00148-9/fulltext#fig3), appendix 1 pp 24–2600148-9/fulltext#supplementary-material); appendix 2 p 300148-9/fulltext#supplementary-material)).

results.title: Novel integration of lateral flow strip and point-of-care isothermal amplification techniques for meat adulteration detection: A comprehensive review - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Novel integration of lateral flow strip and point-of-care isothermal amplification techniques for meat adulteration detection: A comprehensive review. This review critically and objectively examines the recent advancements in meat adulteration detection methods for poultry and livestock products, focusing on integrating LFS devices with isothermal amplification techniques (IATs). Among the available analytical techniques, POC IATs-LFS devices offer high sensitivity and specificity, eliminating the need for thermal cycling instruments and showing great potential for meat adulteration detection at the POC (Grundy et al., 2023; Kim et al., 2023; Y. Unlike previous reviews, which broadly cover IATs or LFS in various applications, our work specifically focuses on the integration of IATs with LFS for meat adulteration detection. To gather relevant literature, we conducted comprehensive searches using the terms "lateral flow strip," "meat adulteration," "isothermal amplification technique," and "animal-species detection technique" in databases such as Web of Science (), PubMed (), and Google Scholar (). Analytical techniques established for detecting meat adulteration range from physical, chemical, anatomical, histological, and biological techniques to sophisticated molecular methods, primarily analyzing species-specific biomarkers such as proteins and DNA in meat samples. The workflow of the IATs-LFS is shown in Fig. 2a and consists of three main steps: (a) rapid extraction and purification of DNA from the targeted meat; (b) onsite DNA amplification using appropriate techniques; and (c) visualization of the LFS results (Kim et al., 2023; Y. PCR is renowned for its high sensitivity, specificity, and widespread application in various fields, including the detection of meat adulteration (Denyingyhot et al., 2022; M. ### Meat authenticity made easy: DNA extraction-free rapid onsite detection of duck and pork ingredients in beef and lamb using dual-recombinase-aided amplification and multiplex lateral flow strips. ### Rapid full-cycle technique to control adulteration of meat products: Integration of accelerated sample preparation, recombinase polymerase amplification, and test-strip detection. * ### A triple lateral flow strip assay based on multiplex polymerase chain reaction for simultaneous detection of chicken, pork and duck in adulterated meat. This study presents a novel multiplex polymerase chain reaction (MPCR)-triple lateral flow strip (TLFS) integrated method, which enables the simultaneous, quantitative detection of chicken, duck, and pork ingredients in adulterated meat samples.

results.title: A New Method Based on LAMP-CRISPR–Cas12a-Lateral Flow Immunochromatographic Strip for Detection
results.content: ##### Social Media Back to Journals » Infection and Drug Resistance » Volume 15 A New Method Based on LAMP-CRISPR–Cas12a-Lateral Flow Immunochromatographic Strip for Detection **Authors**Xu H, Tang H, Li R, Xia Z, Yang W, Zhu Y, Liu Z, Lu G, Ni S, Shen J **Accepted for publication** 27 January 2022 **Published** 27 February 2022 Volume 2022:15 Pages 685—696 **Review by**Single anonymous peer review **Editor who approved publication:**Professor Suresh Antony Huaming Xu,1 Hao Tang,2 Rongrong Li,3 Zhaoxin Xia,2 Wensu Yang,2 Yi Zhu,2 Zhen Liu,2 Guoping Lu,4 Shenwang Ni,2 Jilu Shen 1 1 Department of Laboratory Medicine, The Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University, Hefei, 230012, People’s Republic of China; 2 University Laboratory, The Fourth Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University, Hefei, 230012, People’s Republic of China; 3 The First Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University Laboratory Department, Hefei, Anhui, Peoples’ Republic of China; 4 Laboratory Department of Fuyang Hospital Affiliated to Anhui Medical University, Fuyang, Anhui, People’s Republic of China Correspondence: Jilu Shen, Tel +86 151 5515 2963, Email shenjilu@; 1464675852@qq.com **Introduction:** Carbapenemase-mediated antimicrobial resistance is currently a hot spot of global concern. **Methods:** For this end, we developed a new laboratory assay targeting _Klebsiella pneumoniae_ carbapenemase (KPC) and New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase (NDM) based on loop-mediated isothermal amplification, CRISPR–Cas12a, and lateral flow immunochromatographic strip (CRISPR–Cas-LAMP-lateral flow strip). For the purpose of optimizing the technique, we have tried to develop a novel method based on LAMP-Cas12a-lateral flow immunochromatographic strip, ie, DNA Endonuclease Targeted CRISPR Trans Reporter (DETECTR) for detection of CRE. Biotinylated fluorescein-labeled single-stranded DNA was trans-cleaved by Cas12a and captured by immunochromatographic strip to produce the target band.23 ### Validation of DETECTR for KPC/NDM Detection in Clinical Samples Sensitivity test of colony number of carbapenem producing bacteria. The KPC/NDM carbapenemase-nonproducing samples did not display visible test lines within an hour for LAMP and ∼2 h for PCR-based Cas12a assays.24 As illustrated in Figure 3C, PCR/LAMP amplification also corroborated with the DETECTR assay results. Overall, unlike previously reported methods, such as stand-alone PCR and LAMP, and other CRISPR-based assays, which require expensive materials such as electrophoretic, fluorescence apparatus, and monoclonal antibodies, our method was quick and convenient with inexpensive readout.25 Hence, it is applicable for on-site analysis of nucleic acids in samples with greatly enhanced detection efficiency and convenience.26 ### Specificity of DETECTR in Detection of KPC/NDM Different clinical samples were used to evaluate and validate the specificity of DETECTR assay. We designed and developed a new technique based on CRISPR–Cas12a and combined with LAMP to meet the needs for rapid and affordable diagnostic tools.31 This technique enables us to couple with a lateral flow immunochromatographic strip to develop a rapid test for detecting carbapenemases in clinical samples within 30–40 minutes.

results.title: Rapid On-Site Detection Method for White Spot Syndrome Virus Using Recombinase Polymerase Amplification Combined With Lateral Flow Test Strip Technology - PMC
results.content: # Rapid On-Site Detection Method for White Spot Syndrome Virus Using Recombinase Polymerase Amplification Combined With Lateral Flow Test Strip Technology. Now, some new detection methods have emerged, such as the rapid detection of WSSV using lateral flow technology combined with phage-displayed peptides as biorecognition probes (Kulabhusan et al., 2017) and the electrochemical detection of WSSV using silicone rubber disposable electrodes embedded with graphene quantum dots and gold nanoparticles (Takemura et al., 2020). The study wanted to achieve rapid on-set detection of WSSV by combining RPA amplification with lateral flow test strips. The RPA-LFS detection of the reverse primer and probe showed that amplification occurred in the negative control ( **Figure 4B** , left), Therefore, at the continuous base, the probe and the reverse primer mismatch two bases, respectively. Therefore, RPA-LFS is suitable for WSSV detection with good specificity and no false-positive results. Therefore, the results of this study show that the LFS method is more sensitive than agarose gel electrophoresis, and the detection limit of the RPA-LFS was 20 copies/reaction. For example, qPCR technology can detect up to 12 copies per sample of WSSV (Mendoza-Cano and Sánchez-Paz, 2013), and the detection limit of insulated isothermal PCR (iiPCR) is 17 copies/reaction (Tsai et al., 2014); the detection limit of real-time quantitative LAMP is 100 copies of template DNA (Mekata et al., 2009); real-time RPA can detect WSSV in 5 copies/μl (Xia et al., 2014); and the CRISPR-based SHERLOCK method realizes the single-copy detection of WSSV (Sullivan et al., 2019). Therefore, this study believes that the WSSV detection method provided by RPA-LFS technology has high specificity and sensitivity and can be applied to rapid detection in the field. results.title: Frontiers | Visual detection and differentiation of porcine epidemic diarrhea virus wild−type strains and attenuated vaccine strains using CRISPR/Cas13a-based lateral flow strip
results.content: # Visual detection and differentiation of porcine epidemic diarrhea virus wild−type strains and attenuated vaccine strains using CRISPR/Cas13a-based lateral flow strip. In this study, the CRISPR/Cas13a system was combined with recombinase aided amplification to develop a rapid diagnostic method to distinguish PEDV wild-type strains from attenuated vaccine strains. They can be combined with recombinase aided amplification (RAA) with CRISPR/Cas13a detection to establish specific high sensitivity enzymatic reporter unlocking (SHERLOCK) (Kellner et al., 2019). To construct a more convenient method to detect and distinguish PEDV attenuated vaccine strains from wild-type virus strains, in the present study we developed a detection system by combining CRISPR/Cas13a, RAA, and lateral flow strips. The CRISPR/Cas13a lateral flow detection could detect 1 × 101 copies/µL of DNA in the reaction when the amount of RAA amplification product was increased from 1 µL to 2 µL, which was the detection limit of this method (Figure 3C). To evaluate the specificity of Cas13a lateral flow detection, the established method was used to assess the specificity detection of the PEDV wild-type and vaccine strain, as well as other porcine pathogens, including PCV2, PCV3, PRRSV, PRV, and CSFV. To validate the reliability of the Cas13a lateral flow detection in PEDV wild-type strains from vaccine strains in clinical samples, 42 qRT-PCR-tested tissue samples collected from different farms were detected by Cas13a lateral flow. These data indicated that Cas13a lateral flow detection had high specificity and sensitivity in diagnostic performance for PEDV and could be used for on-site clinical PEDV detection. The crRNA was designed for the ORF3 deletion region to establish a clinical rapid CRISPR/Cas13a lateral flow detection method. In summary, the CRISPR/Cas13a lateral flow detection was established to identify PEDV classic attenuated vaccine strains and wild-type strains. Reverse transcription-enzymatic recombinase amplification coupled with CRISPR-Cas12a for rapid detection and differentiation of PEDV wild-type strains and attenuated vaccine strains. Keywords: PEDV wild-type strain, attenuated vaccine strain, CRISPR/Cas13a, RAA, lateral flow detection. Citation: Yin D, Yin L, Guo H, Wang J, Shen X, Zhao R, Pan X and Dai Y (2022) Visual detection and differentiation of porcine epidemic diarrhea virus wild−type strains and attenuated vaccine strains using CRISPR/Cas13a-based lateral flow strip.
